name: QuickBooks Online
summary: QuickBooks uses OAuth 2.0; you must create an app in the Intuit Developer Portal, set redirect URIs, and exchange the auth code for tokens. The main gate is creating the app and selecting the QuickBooks Online Accounting scope.

oauth_note.text: Supports standard OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow (with optional PKCE) and OpenID Connect extensions.

app_types.name: OAuth App
app_types.when_to_use: Any integration that needs to call QuickBooks Online APIs on behalf of a user

registration_access_claim.text: Anyone can sign in to the Intuit Developer Portal and create an app.

prerequisites.text: Select the QuickBooks Online Accounting scope when creating the app

steps.title: Sign in to the Intuit Developer Portal
steps.detail: Go to https://developer.intuit.com/dashboard and log in with your Intuit credentials.

steps.title: Create a new app
steps.detail: Click “Create an app”, give it a name, and choose “QuickBooks Online Accounting” as the scope.

steps.title: Add redirect URIs
steps.detail: In the app settings, under “Set app redirect URIs”, enter the HTTPS URL(s) your agent will use to receive the auth code (exact match required).

steps.title: Copy client ID and client secret
steps.detail: After saving, note the generated client ID and client secret; they will be used to build the authorization URL and token request.

steps.title: Build the authorization URL
steps.detail: Use the OAuth 2.0 endpoint https://appcenter.intuit.com/connect/oauth2 with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope (e.g. com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting), and optional code_challenge for PKCE.

steps.title: Exchange code for tokens
steps.detail: POST to https://oauth.platform.intuit.com/oauth2/v1/tokens/bearer with grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri, client_id, client_secret (or PKCE verifier). Store access and refresh tokens.

steps.title: Test with the OAuth Playground (optional)
steps.detail: Open https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/playground and run through the flow using your app’s credentials to verify tokens.

approval_claim.text: The provided docs do not describe a review or approval step for publishing an app.

unreviewed_limits.text: You can use sandbox companies and the OAuth Playground without any review; production calls work once you have valid client credentials.

approval_wait.note: Docs do not mention a review timeline.

redirect_uri_rules.text: Must be HTTPS (except localhost for development); the URI must match exactly one of the entries in the app’s redirect list.

token_lifecycle.text: Access tokens are short‑lived (typically 1 hour); refresh tokens are long‑lived and can be used to obtain new access tokens. Refresh tokens can be revoked via the developer portal.

scopes_note.text: Scopes are identified by strings like com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting; select the QuickBooks Online Accounting scope when creating the app. No incremental auth documented.

pkce_required.text: PKCE is supported but not required; recommended for public clients.

blockers.fix: Add an HTTPS URL to the app’s redirect list; localhost is only allowed for testing.
Upgrade to TLS 1.2 or higher as TLS 1.0/1.1 are deprecated.
Use the exact scope name provided (e.g., com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting).

agent_can: exchange authorization code for access/refresh tokens
store credentials for later API calls
human_must: log in to the Intuit Developer Portal
create the app and set redirect URIs
obtain client secret (cannot be retrieved programmatically)

agent_attempts.result: No discovery document. Normal for many providers; endpoints must come from docs.
